title.en: Rivers and coasts (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en:
Seema lives in a village on the bank of the Kaveri river. Her cousin Joe lives in a fishing village by the sea.
Seema's family grows rice with river water. Joe's family catches fish and dries them on the beach.
"Water gives us work and food," they both agreed.

A river is a large stream of water that flows from high land towards the sea. Rivers give water for drinking and farming, fish for food, transport by boat and fertile soil on their banks. Many old cities grew beside rivers.
A coast is the land next to the sea. Coastal people fish, make salt, run ports and work in tourism. Ports send goods to other countries and bring goods from them.
Rivers and coasts need care. Dirty water and plastic waste harm river and sea life, so we must keep them clean.
A river flows from high land to the sea. It gives water, fish and fertile soil.
Rivers also help travel by boat. Many old cities grew beside rivers.
A coast is the land beside the sea. People there fish, make salt and run ports.
We must keep rivers and seas clean.

problem.en: Why do farmers like to live near rivers?

text.en: Floods leave fertile soil on the banks.
So crops grow well near rivers.

why.en: That is why many villages are on river banks.

prompt.en: A friend says it is fine to throw plastic into a river because it flows away. How will you explain?

requiredIdeas.en: The plastic harms fish and ends up in the sea.
The same water is used by people downstream.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking rivers can carry waste away safely.

points.en: Rivers give water, fish, fertile soil and transport.
Coastal people fish, make salt and run ports.
We must keep rivers and seas clean.
